message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day battles in European history.  Casualty figures vary depending on the source and how “casualties” are defined (killed, wounded, missing, captured).  A commonly cited estimate is:

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| **French** | ~25 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |
| **Allied (British, Dutch, Belgian, Prussian)** | ~22 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |

These totals include both killed and wounded, as well as those taken prisoner or reported missing.  Some historians give slightly higher or lower numbers—for example, the French may have suffered up to 30 000 casualties, while Allied losses are sometimes quoted as 20 000–23 000.  The key point is that roughly half a million soldiers were engaged, and the battle cost about 47 000–50 000 men in total casualties.
